analysis.title: China: Three things in China
key_insights: The PBOC announced on November 3 that it would raise the reserve requirement ratio on FX deposits from 2% to 4%, tightening FX liquidity and weakening the CNY against the USD. GS reads it as a signal that policymakers were uncomfortable with the speed of CNY appreciation.

In the month before the announcement, the CNY had appreciated against the USD at an annualized pace of around 10%. USDCNY fell below 6.65 on November 2 and jumped to 6.67 on the day of the announcement.
GS expects Chinese authorities to resist rapid CNY appreciation and to prefer a gradual pace of strengthening, such as 3-5% per year against the USD.

GS US economists see Democratic wins in both the House and Senate as unlikely to change the federal outlook for data center and AI regulation. Democratic wins at the state and local level are likely to lead to short-term data center moratoria that could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.

The moratoria could weigh somewhat on Chinese exports next year through less overseas AI-related demand. GS remains constructive on Chinese exports because the US economists expect the moratoria to be temporary and because AI-related products have not been the key driver of Chinese real export growth.

The November 6 State Council meeting, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, followed up on President Xi's remarks on the first three quarters' economic situation. Its pledges to 'improve market stabilization mechanisms' and 'enhance the inherent stability of the stock market' suggest recent equity volatility has caught top leadership's attention.

The State Council's pledges to 'carefully study the approach for next year's economic work' and to 'strengthen the continuity of policies across years' suggest some of this year's funding resources may be spent early next year to support growth stability, since the 2026 growth target appears within reach.
